power.capacity-scope: the load the PDU can hand on, 11 kW (the "Output kW" column of the maker's table). It is not what the PDU draws itself

occupant-attrs.data-description: ETH2 and ETH1, the two redundant network jacks
ETH2 and ETH1, the two redundant network jacks
the CAN bus jack for CMC III sensors
the USB port for firmware updates and data logging

configs.description: The PDU as it ships: the fixed cord and the two push-button attachments on it. The connector lock for IEC C14 and C20 connectors, the universal mounting kit and the mounting adaptor are not drawn.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: the two sources disagree. The data sheet says black anodised RAL 9005 ("other colours may be configured"), drawn as #0e0e10. The photographs of the metered family show a natural silver-grey extrusion, median #8a8a8a over 383777 pixels of photograph 78_2802, and dark graphite plates. Black is drawn, as the data sheet states. Nine of the ten basic Rittal devices on main draw silver, #b9bbbe.
gaps.wanted: a rating plate or order note naming the finish of this SKU.

gaps.note: photograph 78_3236 shows a small module with two sockets, two arrows and dots at the foot end of one phase of a three-phase strip. No held document says which listed SKU carries it, so it is not drawn.
gaps.wanted: a document that names the SKU and draws the module.

gaps.note: fig. 21 item 12 calls the jack a "CAN bus connection (daisy chain) for CMC III sensors, 24 V, 1 A". The instructions state no bit rate for it. It carries no speed and the search is recorded here.
gaps.wanted: the maker's word on the CAN bus bit rate.

gaps.note: no photograph of this SKU shows what is printed beside the outlets. The placement ids stand.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the printed outlet numbers.

gaps.note: the phase frames are drawn in the colours of photograph 78_2802. Their width is estimated from three sample lines. The plates of phase 1 and phase 2 touch, as the drawing's cell lines give them.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of the front with a scale.

gaps.note: the front view draws the cord and its plug across the first phase group. The cell lines of its first block of C13 are hidden, so the block is set from the next one.
gaps.wanted: a front view with the cord drawn away.

gaps.note: the mounting adaptor 7000.688 and the universal mounting kit are named and not drawn.

gaps.wanted: one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power` (profile `power` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
no bays and no grouped ports to correlate against, so there is nothing to wire yet - group the ports first - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

breakers.note: datasheet - dri1308088en p.1 gives circuit-breakers only for 32 A versions. This SKU is 16 A and the circuit diagram draws none. No breaker is drawn and none is stated.

button-plates.note: The plan view of page 20 draws each button plate 25.0 along the strip and 35.0 across. Two lines stand 5.0 mm in from its ends and three rings, 15.0, 7.5 and 3.7 across, sit at its centre. They are the part rittal/pdu-metered-button@1, read from the vector paths. Two lines of 24.0 mm cross at its centre, one across the strip and one along it, under the rings. The label cover carries its double rim, read the same way.

c13-frames.note: Each C13 of the front view of page 20 sits in a rounded outer frame, 28.0 along the strip and 35.8 across, with R2.5 corners. It is drawn here as decor. Neighbouring frames stand 28.35 apart and nearly touch. The frames were read from the page's vector paths, twice. std/c13-outlet@1 draws the well, nose and contacts inside each frame. The six C13 under the plug have no frame in the drawing, so theirs are estimated at the outlet centres. The outlets stand up to 0.59 mm from their frame centre and are not moved. Pages 3 and 18 give the well chamfers of 6.5 mm and the nose 5.0 mm, read twice at the upper and lower corner. The shared part draws 5.4 and 4.5, so its diagonals stand 0.78 and 0.37 mm from the drawing's. The well's corner stands 3.1 mm from the frame's end and 2.9 mm from its side. Decor has no chamfer or polyline shape (device.schema.json line 1496 lists `rect`, `d-sub` and `slot`) and the part is shared, so they are not changed.

c19-frames.note: Each C19 of the front view of page 20 sits in two rounded frames. The outer one is 42.1 along the strip and 34.11 across, with R1.5 corners, and is drawn here. The inner one is 34.7 by 26.7 with R4.5 corners, 3.65 mm inside it. It is the mouth that std/c19-outlet@1 draws at 35.6 by 27.7, so it is not drawn twice. The two C19s of a pair are 42.5 mm apart in the drawing, so each stands at its frame's centre. The outer frames were read from the page's vector paths and from a 1800 dpi render.

cell-lines.note: The front view of page 20 draws full-height lines across the strip at the ends of each block of outlets. They are drawn as 0.2 mm lines, or 0.35 mm where the drawing doubles a line 0.2 mm apart. They were read from the vector paths. Between two C13 the drawing has no line, only the frames.

chassis.note: drawing - length 1895 (the dimension of the front view and the table of page 1). Width is 44 (the data sheet's "44 mm (1 U)"), depth 72.1 (the side view's dimension). The data sheet (dri1308088en, p.1) prints "PDU enclosure depth 70 mm" and the end view 109. The 109 is the body with the cable gland standing out of the front and the button out of the back. The 70 is the extrusion profile. 72.1 is drawn, as on the basic devices.

colour.note: The data sheet (dri1308088en, p.1) says "Aluminium, anodised in RAL 9005 (black, other colours may be configured)", so the body is drawn black. The screen value #0e0e10 is the usual one for RAL 9005 and is estimated. The two photographs of the metered family show a natural silver-grey extrusion, median #8a8a8a over 383777 pixels of photograph 78_2802. They also show dark graphite plates, #2b2b2c over 301257 pixels. Colours are a later touch. The gap below names both.

controller.note: drawing - the controller cell is 1171.53 to 1371.56 of page 20, between phase 2 and phase 3. Its parts are the PDU controller plate and two RJ45 jacks (ETH2 and ETH1). The rest are an RJ12 jack (RS232), an RJ45 jack (CAN bus), a USB-A port and two small headers. They are read as the DK 7979.238 page reads them, and the cell lines agree to 0.3 mm. Rittal, "Montage-, Installations- und Betriebsanleitung" for the PDU metered (7979204), fig. 21 names each of them. The positions follow the drawing, rotated so the foot is down.

dcim.note: the input is one power port from the cord part and each outlet a power outlet it feeds. C13 and C19 export as the IEC types. The CEE plug exports as `other` with a label. The jacks export as ports of their own type.

end-views.note: The end view of page 20 draws the 44.0 by 72.1 mm section of the body, plain. Its outline is drawn on the top and the bottom face. The gland, the cover and the button stand outside the section, 109 mm in all. They are not drawn on the face, for the reason given for the side views. The view does not tell the two ends apart, so both are built from it.

front.note: drawing - the front view of page 20, mm from the foot end. The foot cell is 0 to 72.1 with the gland ring. The cord cell runs to 195.4 with a raised label cover in it. A blank cell runs to 223.8. Phase 1 is 223.8 to 675.46, phase 2 is 675.46 to 1127.14, a spacer runs to 1171.53, and the controller runs to 1371.56. A spacer runs to 1415.96, phase 3 is 1415.96 to 1867.9, and the head cap runs to 1895. Each phase is two blocks of six C13 cells, 180.4 long, and one cell of two C19, 90.8 long. Outlets count from the foot. The C13 long axis is across the strip and the C19 long axis along it.

head-cap-ribs.note: The head cap in the front view of page 20 has two full-width lines, at 10.05 and 17.25 mm from the head end. Each is a pair of lines 0.2 mm apart and is drawn as one 0.35 mm line. They were read from the page's vector paths and from a 1800 dpi render. The photographs are too small to count them.

hidden-cells.note: The front view draws the cord and its plug across the first phase group. The first block of six C13 cells lies under the plug. Its lines are estimated from the next block, 180.41 long, which ends at the 404.19 line that shows. The blank cell before it is the 28.4 left over.

input.note: datasheet - dri1308088en p.1 gives 230 V per phase (400 V, 3~) and 16 A for this SKU. It gives five wires and a 3 m cable of type H05-VV. The circuit diagram draws the neutral to each phase group, so each outlet is line to neutral. The unit has a fixed cord and no inlet. `plug-rating-a` is not written, as the data sheet rates the unit and not the plug.

label-cover.note: The label cover in the cord cell is the part rittal/pdu-cover-plate@1. The front view gives its rectangle. The side view of page 18 draws it as a trapezoid 13.2 mm proud, read at 600 and 1200 dpi. The part builds the sloped ends.

lamps.note: Instructions p.18 to 19, tables 1 to 4. Every lamp is drawn dark and states its colours. POWER is green. The multi-LED STATUS lamp is green, orange or red. It is blue for a changed position and white for a sensor update. Two flashing codes cycle colours in the table. Device-detected cycles green, orange and red. Device-lost alternates red and blue. Each is stated here as one colour, green and red, which is a single-colour approximation of the printed cycle. The CAN jack has a green and a red lamp and each Ethernet jack a green and an orange one. The two CAN lamps are estimated and stand 1.6 mm toward the head, so neither straddles the plate's section line. The drawing shows no lamp there. Fig. 21 shows no lit lamp. Its green #3baa39 over 2251 pixels is the ETH1 jack body. Its yellow #f0f130 over 287 pixels is a contact pad, in a 200 dpi render of page 18. The lit colours here are the library's usual values, estimated.

lifecycle.note: the maker's page lists the SKU among the metered variants. No end-of-life notice was found in the pages read.

logo.note: The RITTAL mark is drawn on the controller plate from fig. 21. Its size is not printed and is estimated.

method.note: FIGURES FROM THE MAKER'S DIMENSIONED DRAWING. Rittal, "Technical details, Power Distribution Unit, Metered version" (dri2108029en, 08.2023), PDF page 20, DK 7979.240. The page has a plan view, a side view, an end view and a front view, with the circuit diagram below. The cell lines of the front view were read from a 600 dpi render at the drawing's own scale. The 1895 overall length reads 1.937 px per mm. Each cell edge is a full-height line. Good to about 1 mm. Each outlet sits in its housing at the lines the drawing shows inside the block.

mount.note: `rack-side`, the library's way to say a part stands vertically beside an upright. It hangs on the two push-button attachments of the plan view, dimensioned 1600.2 apart. The data sheet's "PDU mounting options" are the enclosure frame at the side of the 482.6 mm mounting frame and the cable route. The mounting adaptor 7000.688 is an accessory and is not drawn. `ru: 43` is the 1895 mm it runs, 1895 / 44.45 = 42.6.

mounting-buttons.note: drawing - the plan view of page 20 shows two buttons 1600.2 apart (dimensioned). Their plates read 134.99 to 159.77 and 1735.23 to 1760.01 from the foot end, 25.2 long. The foot end of the plan view is taken to be the end of the front view's foot cell.

outlets.note: datasheet and drawing - the table of page 1 ("PDU metered") lists DK 7979.240. It gives 3~, 16 A, 11 kW, CEE input, 36 IEC C13 and 6 IEC C19, measuring per phase, 1895 mm. The circuit diagram draws six IEC C13, six IEC C13 and two IEC C19 on each of L1, L2 and L3. std/c13-outlet@1 and std/c19-outlet@1. None is switched and none has a lamp. NO OUTLET NAME IS WRITTEN. No held photograph is of this SKU and the outlets keep their placement ids, counted from the foot.

phase-plates.note: The instructions (7979204) mark the phases "L1: pink, L2: black, L3: white". They do so in the table of technical data and in the section on phases and slots. The data sheet (dri1308088en, p.1) says "Pink, black, white". The metered drawing document (dri2108029en) states neither. Photograph 78_2802 shows this layout. The pink reads #ee488f over 15335 pixels and the white #fefefe over 15569 pixels. Both show as a thin margin round each outlet block. Three sample lines run across the strip, 81 px for the 44 mm face. They read the pink margin at 1.1 mm on the far side and 5.8 mm on the near side. The white reads about 12 px on the far side. Each is drawn as a frame 3.5 mm wide, the mean, round each block of the drawing's cell lines, on a dark plate. The width is estimated. The frame's inner edge reaches 1.7 to 2.6 mm into the outermost C13 or C19 frame at a block end. The drawing shows no phase frame, and the photograph reads the margin at 1.1 to 5.8 mm, so the overlap is inside what was measured. The outlet frame line is drawn over the pink band. The black plate is not sampled and is drawn #1f1f21 as the basic family is.

plan-circles.note: The plan view of page 20 shows four small circles on the centre line, at 191.9, 458.7, 1436.4 and 1703.2 mm from the foot. They read 2.4 mm across, twice at 600 dpi. Nothing says what they are. They are drawn on the back as dark discs, each marked as estimated.

plate-outline.note: The controller plate steps in by 0.6 mm on each side over the last 23.0 mm of each end. An inner rim line runs 1.4 mm inside each end section. Both are read from a 1800 dpi render of page 18. The foot end is drawn by the device and the head end by the controller part.

plate-sections.note: The controller plate in the front view of page 20 has five full-height section lines. They are at 74.0, 104.0, 131.0, 142.7 and 160.0 mm from the head end of the plate. They were read from the vector paths and from a 1800 dpi render. The first is in rittal/pdu-controller@1 and the other four are drawn here.

ports.note: fig. 21 items 9 to 15. ETH2 (white body) is left of ETH1 (green body). RS232 is left of CAN bus and the USB port is below. The data sheet calls the RS232 port RJ12. The library's `rj11` key is the same six-position body, so the RS232 jack is the RJ11 jack part. Each jack is drawn unrotated with its pins up.

rear.note: drawing - the plan view of page 20 draws two grooves 3.0 wide and a ridge 1.55 wide with a line along its crest. It also draws two buttons. The grooves and the ridge run 1575.2 mm between the plates, from 159.89 to 1735.09 from the head end. They also run from each strip end to its plate. The head run starts 3.51 mm from the head end. The foot run stops 3.0 mm short of the foot end. They were read from the vector paths, twice. The mid circles are drawn by the `mark-N` entries.

side-views.note: The side view of page 20 draws the body as a 72.1 by 1895 rectangle. Its front edge has a notch, 2.1 mm deep and 0.18 to 0.34 wide, at each cell line. The outline and the notches were read from the vector paths, twice, and are drawn as decor. The gland, the label cover, the outlet bars and the two button feet stand outside that rectangle, past the face. Decor is clipped to the face (L150) and the depth stays 72.1, so they are not drawn on it. The cover and the buttons stand out in 3D as the relief of their parts. The drawing shows one side and the other is built the same, mirrored.

usb-port.note: The data sheet (dri1308088en, p.1) calls the port "USB 2.0 port (USB-A)", so it is std/usb-a@1 in its white-tongue skin. Fig. 21 item 15 and photograph 78_2802 show a silver-white shell and no trident. The shell reads #c5c5c5 over 309 pixels of a 200 dpi render of page 18. It is drawn as a plate behind the port, as the device's own decor. No shared part draws a USB-A metal shell, and the white-tongue part is reused for the tongue. The shell takes its place and size from the vector paths, 12.5 by 5.13 mm. The part's tongue is 10.2 mm wide against 11.1 drawn, so its centre stands on the drawn centre.
